previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure was admitted for left ear pain and swelling concerning for malignant otitis externa. Imaging showed soft tissue induration without bone erosion, and she was treated for cellulitis with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to linezolid and ciprofloxacin with oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis. Her hospital course was complicated by sepsis, acute kidney injury with hyperkalemia, and anion gap metabolic acidosis, all of which improved with supportive care. Her home lisinopril was held, insulin regimen adjusted, and carvedilol and atorvastatin initiated for cardioprotection. She responded well, with infection resolution, renal recovery, and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up, lab monitoring, and a plan to complete antibiotics and restart medications as directed.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with end-stage renal disease, considering
hemodialysis for venous mapping for possible fistula creation.

COMPARISON:  None.

BILATERAL UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND:  Grayscale and color Doppler examination
was performed of the right and left upper extremity venous system.

On the right, the basilic vein is patent and measures 0.24 cm in the mid
forearm, 0.23 cm in the antecubital fossa, and 0.20 cm in the upper arm. 
There is no intraluminal thrombus.  The right cephalic vein is patent
throughout its course and measures 0.18 cm in the distal forearm, 0.36 cm in
the antecubital fossa, and 0.11 cm in the upper arm.  There is phasic flow
within the right subclavian vein.

The right brachial artery demonstrates significant calcification and measures
0.19 cm in diameter.  The right renal artery measures 0.18 cm and also
demonstrates significant calcification.

On the left, the basilic vein is patent and measures 0.24 cm in the mid
forearm, 0.40 cm in the antecubital fossa, and 0.28 cm in the upper arm.  The
cephalic vein is patent only in the distal forearm measuring 0.19-0.23 cm. 
The left subclavian vein demonstrates phasic waveform.  The left brachial
artery measures 0.3 cm with significant calcification and the left renal
artery demonstrates 0.2 cm with some calcification.  Both of these demonstrate
appropriate arterial waveforms.

IMPRESSION:  Bilateral cephalic and basilic veins are described above.
